h1:
Khao Yai Attractions
Park, Waterfalls, Vineyards & Mountain Cafes
intro: Khao Yai (Pak Chong district, Nakhon Ratchasima) is the easy escape from Bangkok that works year-round — it's only about a 2.5–3 hour drive away. What makes it special is the variety packed into one area: green forest inside the national park, big waterfalls, vineyards where you can taste wine, European-style villages, farms where you feed animals, and mountain-view cafes where you can sip coffee in the cool air all day. We've gathered the spots that are actually open right now, with entry fees and opening hours so it's easy to plan.

blocks.html: Khao Yai's attractions split roughly into two zones: inside Khao Yai National Park (nature, waterfalls, viewpoints, wildlife) and outside the park along Thanarat Road in Pak Chong, which is packed with vineyards, sheep farms, European villages, flower gardens and mountain-view cafes. Most people give each zone its own day, since a trip into the park eats up almost the whole day.

Khao Yai National Park is a UNESCO natural World Heritage Site — a huge forest spanning four provinces, with nature trails, viewpoints, waterfalls and the chance to spot wildlife like deer, barking deer and wild elephants. There are two main entrances: the Nern Hom checkpoint (Prachinburi side) and the Sao Chao Pho checkpoint (Pak Chong side). Entry for Thai adults is around 40 THB, children 20 THB, plus roughly 30–50 THB per car (prices can change, so double-check on site). The park has started using the QueQ app to buy tickets in advance and cut down on queues at the gate.

items.name: Heo Suwat Waterfall
items.blurb: Khao Yai's most famous waterfall, dropping about 20 metres off a cliff face. It's a short walk down from the car park. In the rainy season the flow is heavy and gorgeous, but the path gets slippery, so take extra care.

items.name: Heo Narok Waterfall
items.blurb: The tallest waterfall in Khao Yai, dropping in several tiers. You'll walk down a fair number of steps to reach the viewpoint — tiring but worth it. An elephant once fell here, so there are fences and warning signs. Don't cross the barriers.

items.name: Pha Kluai Mai / Khao Khiao viewpoints
items.blurb: Viewpoints for the sea of fog and sunrise. On cold-season mornings the mist rolls in beautifully. Nearby are the Pha Kluai Mai and Lam Takhong campgrounds.

items.name: Nature trails
items.blurb: Several routes to suit your energy level, from short loops around the visitor centre to longer trails best done with a ranger. Great for anyone who likes hiking and birdwatching.

blocks.title: Drive safely inside the park
blocks.html: The roads inside the park are winding, and wildlife can cross at any time — especially from late afternoon into the evening. Drive slowly and stay under the speed-limit signs. If you meet an elephant, stop and wait, switch off your high beams, don't honk, and never feed the wildlife.

blocks.html: Pak Chong–Khao Yai is one of Thailand's wine regions — the climate and soil suit growing wine grapes. Here you'll find vineyards where you can walk and take photos, ride a tram through the rows, and taste wine with the mountains as your backdrop.

items.name: PB Valley Khao Yai Winery
items.blurb: The best-known vineyard and winery in Khao Yai. There are vineyard tours with tasting, and a restaurant overlooking the vines (Great Hornbill), open around 09:00–18:00. Tasting tours start in the low hundreds of THB per person — check tour times ahead.

items.name: GranMonte Vineyard
items.blurb: A family-run vineyard with the VINCOTTO restaurant overlooking the vines — a good spot for a lunch with a glass of wine. The atmosphere is warm and relaxed.

items.name: Alcidini / smaller wineries nearby
items.blurb: Along Thanarat Road there are smaller vineyards and cafes making their own wine scattered about — good for a quick photo stop or to grab a small bottle to take home.

blocks.title: Don't drink and drive
blocks.html: Wine tastings are fun, but if you're driving on these winding mountain roads afterward, have someone in your group who isn't drinking take the wheel — or keep the tasting modest.
Khao Yai's most popular photo zone is the European-styled villages and farms where you can feed the animals. They suit families with kids and couples after nice photos.

items.name: Primo Piazza
items.blurb: A Tuscan, Italian-style village with a farm zone of sheep, horses and alpacas you can feed, plus the pretty Primo Cafe. Entry is around 150 THB for adults and 100 THB for children, open roughly 09:00–18:00 (check weekday vs. weekend hours again before you go).

items.name: Palio Khao Yai
items.blurb: An Italian-town-style community mall — walk around for photos, shop for souvenirs, grab coffee or sweets. Free entry, a good stop along the way, right on Thanarat Road.

items.name: Sheep Land
items.blurb: A sheep farm with mountain views where you can feed the sheep, plus seasonal flower fields and plenty of photo spots. Great for bringing kids to play with the animals.

items.name: Farm Chokchai
items.blurb: The legendary dairy farm, with a farm tour to watch cows being milked, a cowboy show, animal feeding, and Umm! Milk ice cream. The free walking zone has restaurants and souvenirs; the farm tour needs a ticket. Open around 09:30–17:00.

items.name: The Bloom by TV Pool
items.blurb: A large flower garden over 100 rai, with blooms rotating by season — the cold season is the prettiest. Lots of photo spots. Entry is around 100 THB on weekdays and 200 THB on weekends.

items.name: Scenical World
items.blurb: A water park and theme park combined, with a range of rides and the Sky Walk viewpoint. Good for families spending the whole day. Open around 10:00–18:00.

items.name: Midwinter Green / seasonal gardens
items.blurb: A garden-and-cafe zone decorated by season — in the cold months they set up flower beds and lights. Nice for an evening stroll and photos.

blocks.html: Another part of Khao Yai's charm is the sheer number of mountain-view cafes, most of them along Thanarat Road and the side lanes climbing up into the hills. You can sit and sip coffee in the cool breeze all day. Here are the ones people talk about most.

items.name: Midwinter Green
items.blurb: A cafe and restaurant overlooking the garden and mountains, decorated in English style, leafy and relaxed — good for lingering. They have coffee, cakes and main dishes.

items.name: GranMonte Vineyard (VINCOTTO)
items.blurb: Sip coffee or wine while looking out over the vines and mountains. Quiet and comfortable — a good spot for a laid-back lunch.

items.name: Cafe in Palio
items.blurb: A coffee-and-dessert spot inside the Italian-style village — wander and take photos, then stop to rest. Free entry, good for a short break.

items.name: Primo Cafe (Primo Piazza)
items.blurb: A cafe in the Tuscan village with views of the sheep farm and pastel buildings — great for photos. Included with Primo Piazza entry.

items.name: Hidden cafes up the hill lanes
items.blurb: Plenty of new cafes have opened along the side lanes climbing into the hills around Pak Chong, many with full-on mountain views. Check the latest reviews before you go, since some open and close by season.

blocks.title: Long weekends get crowded
blocks.html: On weekends and long holidays, Thanarat Road jams up, the popular cafes have long queues, and parking fills. Head out early, start with the spot you most want to see, and book your stay well ahead — places fill up fast.

blocks.text: An Unhurried One-Day Khao Yai Plan

blocks.html: If you only have one day, it's easier to focus on a single zone. Here's a sample plan for the nature + farm/cafe crowd that doesn't rush you.

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.title: Start at the park before the sun gets harsh

items.activity: Leave your hotel and enter via the Sao Chao Pho checkpoint (Pak Chong side)
items.note: An early start dodges the queue at the gate and catches the cool air

items.activity: Stop at the Khao Khiao / Pha Kluai Mai viewpoints + visitor centre
items.note: In the cold season there's a chance of a sea of fog
Wear non-slip shoes — the path gets very wet and slick in the rainy season

blocks.label: Midday
blocks.title: Leave the park for the vineyard side

items.activity: Come down from the hills, lunch at a vineyard-view restaurant (PB Valley or GranMonte)
items.note: Drive down slowly and watch for animals crossing
Check tour times ahead; the driver skips the drinks

blocks.label: Afternoon–Evening
blocks.title: Farm, cafe, and souvenirs to finish

items.activity: Sheep Land or Primo Piazza to feed the animals and take photos
items.note: Families with kids love this zone

items.activity: Sit at a mountain-view cafe in the cool breeze
items.note: Midwinter Green or a cafe in a lane near your hotel

items.activity: Swing by Palio for souvenirs and a stroll with photos
items.note: Free entry, open into the evening

blocks.title: To see it all, stay one night
blocks.html: Khao Yai's attractions are spread out, and driving between zones takes time. If you want both the park and the vineyard–cafe side without rushing, plan to stay at least one night so you can make the most of both morning and evening.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Khao Yai?
faq.a: If you want both the park and the vineyard–farm–cafe side, two days and one night is the sweet spot, since a trip into the park takes almost the whole day. A day trip from Bangkok works too, but you'll have to focus on just one zone.

faq.q: How much is entry to Khao Yai National Park?
faq.a: Thai adults are around 40 THB and children 20 THB, plus roughly 30–50 THB per car. Prices can change, so check on site or buy tickets ahead through the QueQ app to cut down your wait at the gate.

faq.q: What should you watch out for when driving in the park?
faq.a: The roads inside the park are winding and wildlife can cross at any time, especially from late afternoon into the evening. Drive slowly, stay under the speed-limit signs, and if you meet an elephant, stop and wait, switch off your high beams, don't honk, and never feed the wildlife.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Khao Yai?
faq.a: The cold season (Nov–Feb) brings cool air, a chance of a sea of fog, and beautiful flower gardens in bloom — but it's crowded and accommodation fills fast. The rainy season makes the waterfalls full and the scenery lush green, though paths get slippery, so take care. Book your stay ahead on long holidays.

faq.q: Where should you go in Khao Yai with young kids?
faq.a: Animal-feeding farms like Sheep Land, Primo Piazza and Farm Chokchai are kid favourites. The Scenical World theme park has both rides and a water park to keep them busy all day. Skip the longer forest trails in the park if your kids are still small.
